# The pinned CI tools, one row per tool - read by ./install.sh (which installs
# one) and by ../../scripts/check_tool_versions.sh (which reports drift against
# each upstream's latest release). Both reach it through ./lib.sh, so this file
# is the single roster: a tool pinned here cannot go undrift-checked.
#
#   name|pin|kind|url|verify|check
#
# name    the first column an `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-tool` names, and
#         the executable's name - install.sh saves a `raw` download under it,
#         and finds it inside an archive with `find -name <name>`.
# pin     the version, WITHOUT a leading "v" even where upstream's tag has one:
#         some projects tag v1.2.3 but name the asset 1.2.3, and only one
#         placeholder is substituted. The url column carries the literal "v"
#         where the tag needs it. check_tool_versions.sh strips a leading "v"
#         from both sides before comparing, so either convention compares fine.
# kind    raw (a bare executable), tar.gz, tar.xz, cmake (a source tarball
#         this builds - kcov publishes no binary asset), or make (the same,
#         for a ./configure && make tree - mandoc).
# url     %v is the pin. %a is the asset slug for this runner
#         (linux.x86_64 / darwin.aarch64 / darwin.x86_64) and is resolved
#         first, so a version can never be mistaken for one; only shellcheck
#         needs it, being the only tool also installed on macOS.
# verify  the flag install.sh runs the installed tool with as a smoke test.
# check   where to look for the latest release: github:<owner>/<repo>,
#         gitlab:<url-encoded project path> (salsa.debian.org, where
#         checkbashisms lives inside devscripts), or "-" to opt out of the
#         drift report entirely.
#
# Bumping a pin is a hand edit here, and nothing else - the caching action.yml
# reads the version back out of install.sh's `resolve`.
#
# NOTE: .gitignore blankets *.txt and un-ignores this one file by name. A new
# roster file beside it would be swallowed the same way - see dist/'s comment
# at the bottom of .gitignore for the same trap.
shellcheck|0.11.0|tar.xz|https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/download/v%v/shellcheck-v%v.%a.tar.xz|--version|github:koalaman/shellcheck
shfmt|3.14.0|raw|https://github.com/mvdan/sh/releases/download/v%v/shfmt_v%v_linux_amd64|--version|github:mvdan/sh
checkbashisms|2.26.11|raw|https://salsa.debian.org/debian/devscripts/-/raw/v%v/scripts/checkbashisms.pl|--version|gitlab:debian%2Fdevscripts
# actionlint points at kjanat's fork, not upstream rhysd/actionlint: upstream
# is stuck on 1.7.12 and rejects zizmor's `$/...` self-repository syntax
# (rhysd/actionlint#732 open, unmerged); the fork added `$/...` support in
# v1.9.0 and is what unblocks the zizmor pin below.
actionlint|1.14.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint/releases/download/v%v/actionlint_%v_linux_amd64.tar.gz|--version|github:kjanat/actionlint
zizmor|1.30.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/releases/download/v%v/zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|github:zizmorcore/zizmor
nfpm|2.47.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/goreleaser/nfpm/releases/download/v%v/nfpm_%v_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz|--version|github:goreleaser/nfpm
minisign|0.12|tar.gz|https://github.com/jedisct1/minisign/releases/download/%v/minisign-%v-linux.tar.gz|-v|github:jedisct1/minisign
trivy|0.74.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/download/v%v/trivy_%v_Linux-64bit.tar.gz|--version|github:aquasecurity/trivy
hadolint|2.15.1|raw|https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint/releases/download/v%v/hadolint-linux-x86_64|--version|github:hadolint/hadolint
kcov|43|cmake|https://github.com/SimonKagstrom/kcov/archive/refs/tags/v%v.tar.gz|--version|github:SimonKagstrom/kcov
typos|1.50.1|tar.gz|https://github.com/crate-ci/typos/releases/download/v%v/typos-v%v-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz|--version|github:crate-ci/typos
mandoc|1.14.6|make|https://mandoc.bsd.lv/snapshots/mandoc-%v.tar.gz|-T lint -W error /dev/null|-
